statement: The article summarises ISO/IEC 7812: a number has an issuer identification number of 6 to 8 digits, an individual account identifier and one check digit computed with the Luhn algorithm, 8 to 19 digits in total; Visa starts with 4 with 13, 16 or 19 digits; Mastercard starts 51-55 or 2221-2720 with 16 digits; American Express starts 34 or 37 with 15 digits.
location: Article sections on structure and major card networks (section names not recorded)
inference: A digit run longer than 19 digits is not a payment card number; a run that fails the check digit is not a valid one.

notes: That the ISO/IEC 7812 check digit is this exact scheme is stated by the secondary reference, not the patent.

statement: The patent describes a number-verification scheme in which a substitute digit equals twice the original digit plus an end-around carry, summed across digits to detect errors such as transposition.
inference: The check-digit rule used by payment card numbers is the Luhn algorithm; a single altered digit or an adjacent transposition changes the check sum.

notes: Reuse terms of the documentation were not read, so the source stays unresolved for public release.
